text:
maria: seeing p95 spikes between GPU nodes in us-west-2a during the 09:45 batch surge. latency to other GPU hosts jumps from ~1.8ms to ~40-120ms for ~30s windows, qlen/backlog on pods up. Noticed packet retransmits in the infra metrics.
aj: can you paste the short tcpdump/traceroute from one of the affected hosts? also which NIC driver? any recent change to MTU or driver versions?
noah: grabbing tcpdump from gpu-node-17 now. snippet:

# tcpdump -nn -r capture.pcap -tttt 'src host 10.12.3.17 and dst port 5000'
09:45:12.123456 IP 10.12.3.17.5000 > 10.12.3.22.5000: UDP, length 1420
09:45:12.123457 IP (frag) 10.12.3.17 > 10.12.3.22: frag 0:1400@0
09:45:12.123458 IP (frag) 10.12.3.17 > 10.12.3.22: frag 1:20@1400
09:45:12.123460 IP 10.12.3.17.5000 > 10.12.3.22.5000: UDP, length 1420
(then backlog of retransmits)

Looks like fragmentation is present; we also see 'IP (frag)' entries and packets reassembled downstream, with bursts coinciding with the batching window.
kim: checked RDMA counters on the same host (ibdev0): rc_retry_exceeded went from ~0 to 120 during the spike window, and f/w reported link flaps on the switch for the affected ports. ibstat/ibv_devinfo look OK otherwise. Mellanox switch logs show "fragmentation detected" for that port during the timeframe.
dave: did we recently enable jumbo frames or change MTU somewhere? fragmentation + rdma retries makes me think MTU mismatch across path.
maria: we rolled out a kernel NIC offload tweak last week to enable TSO/GSO/GRO on GPU hosts (was trying to improve throughput). Most hosts were set to MTU 9000. One rack (rack-7) still on 1500 due to older ToR config; I bet that's our mismatch.
aj: confirm on gpu-node-17: `ip link show eth0` -> `mtu 9000`, but traceroute to gpu-node-22 shows an intermediate hop with MTU 1500 (from switch fw). also ethtool -k eth0 shows tso/gso/gro = on.
noah: quick mitigation I ran: disabled GRO/GSO/TSO on the NICs for the affected nodes and forced TCP small segments. commands used:
```
ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500   # temporary fallback on nodes where switch enforces 1500
ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
```
After that, observed p95 drop back to ~2-3ms within ~20s.
kim: note disabling offloads increased CPU on those hosts (small bump ~6-8% user), but it's acceptable short-term. RDMA retries went back down after forcing consistent MTU or disabling offloads.
dave: can we do a coordinated rollout? options:
- align MTU across the rack (set ToR to 9000) and ensure all hosts follow (preferred long term)
- or force hosts to 1500 until switch config can be fixed (lower perf but stable)
- or add dynamic routing -> steer batch traffic away from rack-7 during windows (canary rule in robin)
sre-bot: deploy-canary: reroute rule applied -> traffic for /inference-batch to us-west-2a non-rack7 nodes for next 15m :thumbsup:
maria: we'll take two-pronged approach: (1) emergency: keep GSO/GRO/TSO off on impacted hosts until switch team confirms MTU consistency; (2) infra ticket to sync ToR MTU and audit NIC offload policy across all GPU racks. aj you own the MTU audit ticket, kim pls coordinate with cloud provider support about switch logs.
aj: will open Ticket #INF-9482 with steps to validate MTU across all ToRs, collect switch counters, and propose either global 9000 move or global 1500 fallback. also will run rdma stress test overnight targeting rack-7 to verify stability.
noah: added a small temporary autoscale override to reduce concurrent batches to 80% in the affected AZ during the next peak to avoid flaring while we fix.
dave: follow-ups: run a passive pcap collector to capture one full batch window for deeper analysis, and verify NIC firmware levels — older firmware still in rack-7.
maria: thanks all — mitigation in place, monitoring shows p95 stable. I'll post a short postmortem after we have the full capture and ticket updates. :white_check_mark:
